cur:manuscripts-drogo-nativity.summary: Inside the letter D, figures stand above on a rocky height beside the building of Bethlehem, while below, in a curtained chamber, haloed figures attend to the newborn Christ. The miniature accompanies the Christmas prayers of the sacramentary.
facts: The Drogo Sacramentary was written and painted for the personal use of Drogo, Bishop of Metz and a son of Charlemagne; it contains only the prayers spoken by the bishop at Mass through the year.
Its scenes are set inside the initial letters of the prayers, in delicate gold vine-scrolls — an early and influential use of the historiated initial.
cur:manuscripts-drogo-nativity.notes: Folio not stated on the Commons file; the miniature is an initial within the text page. The small figures are worn; the identification follows the Commons title ('Nativité').

cur:manuscripts-stuttgart-psalter-psalm-.summary: Beneath the great initial B of 'Beatus vir', the haloed Christ hangs on the cross with arms outstretched, while two men converse beside him; above, a figure with a cross-staff stands at the opening of the psalm. The psalm's righteous man, 'like a tree planted by the rivers of water', is read as Christ on the tree of the Cross.
facts: The Stuttgart Psalter was made around 820–830 at the abbey of Saint-Germain-des-Prés near Paris; its 168 leaves contain the psalms with 316 coloured miniatures set between the verses they illustrate.
Its pictures interpret the psalms literally, historically or — very often — Christologically, as prophecies of the life of Christ.
cur:manuscripts-stuttgart-psalter-psalm-.notes: Image from the WLB digital facsimile (Public Domain Mark), showing the whole page with the miniature.
